compatibility.title: Which Land Rover Models Use the 30DDTX?
compatibility.intro: The 30DDTX is Land Rover's modern Ingenium 3.0-litre inline-6 diesel, introduced to replace the older V6 306DT. It offers improved refinement, better fuel economy, and a more compact packaging layout, serving as the primary diesel option for Land Rover's mid-size and large SUVs during this period.

costGuide.title: Land Rover 30DDTX Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 30DDTX typically takes 14-18 hours at £65/hr (independent specialist) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The final cost of a Land Rover 30DDTX engine replacement is heavily influenced by the condition of the emissions and forced-induction systems. Units rebuilt with a new or refurbished EGR cooler, updated AdBlue system components, and refreshed turbochargers command a slight premium but prevent near-term repeat failures. For a detailed breakdown of how specific component conditions affect the overall Land Rover 30DDTX engine cost, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Land Rover 30DDTX Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks
items.whatHappens: The EGR cooler can develop internal or external leaks, leading to unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential engine overheating if ignored. This is often exacerbated by carbon buildup in the intake system.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement is a standard maintenance fix. However, if the leak has caused severe overheating, the cylinder head may be compromised, necessitating a full engine replacement. Read our full coolant system failure guide.

items.title: AdBlue System Faults
items.whatHappens: The AdBlue heater or injector can fail, causing the diesel exhaust fluid to crystallize. This leads to "Engine Power Reduced" warnings, fault codes, and eventually a no-start condition once the countdown timer expires.
items.repairVsReplace: Component replacement (heater, injector, or dosing module) is a standard repair and does not typically require a full engine replacement unless the crystallization has severely damaged the SCR catalyst or exhaust plumbing.

items.title: Turbocharger Wear
items.whatHappens: The turbocharger wastegate can develop a rattle, or the bearings can wear over time, leading to boost leaks, reduced power, and excessive smoke.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbocharger replacement or refurbishment is a standard repair and does not require a full engine replacement unless turbo debris has entered the oil system and caused bearing damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: As a newer Ingenium design, the 30DDTX inline-6 architecture avoids the catastrophic crankshaft bearing failures that plagued the older 306DT V6, making it a significantly more robust and reliable platform overall .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 30DDTX
variants.intro: The 30DDTX is Land Rover's specific designation for the modern 3.0-litre Ingenium inline-6 diesel. Confirming your exact code is critical because, while it shares a displacement with older Land Rover diesels, the physical architecture and engine management are entirely different. WHERE TO FIND THE CODE: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover. It will also be explicitly listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Code" or "Engine Capacity", and can be decoded directly from your 17-character VIN. COMMONLY CONFUSED CODES: - 306DT: The older 3.0L V6 diesel. Externally distinct (V6 vs Inline-6), with entirely different mounting points, ECU, and a known history of catastrophic crankshaft bearing failures. - 306D1: Another variant of the older 3.0L V6 architecture, sharing the same fundamental layout and failure risks as the 306DT, and completely non-interchangeable with the inline-6 30DDTX. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The inline-6 architecture of the 30DDTX is physically and electronically incompatible with the V6 306DT/306D1 blocks. Attempting to swap a V6 unit into an inline-6 chassis without extensive, custom fabrication and ECU remapping is not viable. CLOSING LINE: Not 100% sure? buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 30DDTX - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Land Rover 30DDTX engine is only advisable if it comes with a comprehensive, documented service history proving that the AdBlue system and EGR cooler have been proactively maintained or replaced. Without this specific history, the risk of inheriting emissions-related faults is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used Land Rover 30DDTX engine network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Land Rover 30DDTX engine is the most balanced and recommended choice for the majority of owners. A quality, specialist-led rebuild will systematically address the known weak points: a new or refurbished EGR cooler, updated AdBlue dosing components, refreshed turbochargers, and all critical gaskets and seals. This effectively resets the engine's reliability clock and is the most cost-effective way to secure long-term peace of mind. Compare reconditioned Land Rover 30DDTX engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples, vehicles that have suffered from overheating, or if the cylinder bores show measurable scoring. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, a reground crankshaft, and a complete refresh of the oil pump, ensuring the engine can reliably handle another 100,000+ miles of heavy-duty use. View rebuilt Land Rover 30DDTX engine specifications.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Buying through the EnginesMarket network means you can opt for a full supply and fit service, with the replacement engine installed by a Land Rover specialist and backed by a nationwide warranty. Learn more about supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The Land Rover 30DDTX is typically found in host vehicles (like the Discovery 5 L462 or Range Rover Sport L494 facelift) valued between £15,000 and £45,000+, heavily dependent on condition, mileage, and specification. For these modern, high-value chassis, a £6,500+ reconditioned Land Rover 30DDTX engine replacement represents a viable investment (well under 50% of the vehicle's total current market value), making replacement financially sound compared to older, lower-value platforms.

items.question: How much does a Land Rover 30DDTX engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Land Rover 30DDTX engine typically costs between £6,500 and £9,500 for supply only. items.question: What is the most common failure with the 30DDTX?
items.answer: The most common failures are EGR cooler leaks and AdBlue system faults, typically emerging between 60,000 and 100,000 miles. EGR leaks can lead to unexplained coolant loss, while AdBlue crystallization triggers 'Engine Power Reduced' warnings. Turbocharger wear is also a documented issue at higher mileages.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the 30DDTX engine?
items.answer: The 30DDTX was fitted to the Land Rover Discovery 5 (L462) and the facelifted Range Rover Sport (L494) between 2016 and 2020. It serves as the primary 3.0L diesel option, replacing the older V6 architecture. It offers improved refinement and better fuel economy for these heavy SUV platforms.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 30DDTX engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Land Rover 30DDTX is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the complexity and high replacement cost of the turbo and emissions systems. A proper rebuild will systematically replace the EGR cooler, AdBlue dosing components, and turbochargers. A used unit is only advisable with comprehensive, documented proof that these specific preventative repairs have already been completed.
